title: SR-1.03 Replay protection that survives a restart
request: Closes G03: The nonce cache is in-memory, so a daemon restart reopens the five-minute replay window. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: none.

tasks.title: Persisted nonce cache
requirements: nonces seen in the skew window are persisted (0600) and reloaded on start
the store is bounded by the window and pruned

the nonce is recorded durably before the request's handler runs, so before any side effect and before the response: the store is read synchronously inside createServer, before it returns, and each use is written through atomically (write to a temporary file, then rename) with mode 0600 set on every write, and use() stays synchronous so one process cannot accept a nonce twice

the cache is keyed by the device's public key and the nonce (the bearer token is not part of the signed payload, so keying by token would let a rotated token reopen the window, and two device records holding one key share one window); a nonce is recorded only after the proof verifies
a failure to persist the nonce fails closed: the request is refused with a 5xx and the nonce stays recorded in memory so a replay is still refused; no try and catch swallows the write error
every write reads the store on disk, merges it with the in-memory set, prunes and writes the result, so two servers on one vault never lose each other's nonces

pruning is by age only: an entry is dropped only once now minus its signed timestamp exceeds the skew window, so a request with that timestamp could no longer be accepted; a clock that steps backward never drops an entry; no count cap ever evicts a nonce that is still inside the window, and the store is pruned while the daemon runs, not only at load

an unreadable store (EACCES) or a store of the wrong shape is renamed aside (to <store>.damaged-<time>) with a message naming the file, and the new store records a not-before time equal to the moment the damage was found; every signed request whose timestamp is earlier is refused as already used, across restarts, until that time is older than the skew window; fresh requests are served, and the daemon never treats the damage as a first run and never crash-loops
no per-device last-timestamp guard: requests signed out of order inside the window are accepted once each

a write fault is answered 5xx with a body that names neither the vault root nor .memev, and the nonce stays recorded in memory, so the same request is refused as already used while the fault lasts; no flush on close stands in for the write
the store loader accepts only its own shape and treats anything else ('[]', '{}', a string, true, nulls inside) as damaged; it never throws inside createServer
use() re-reads the store when its mtime changed since it last read it, so a request another process accepted is refused here

criteria.statement: Test 'replay after a killed daemon restart'. Set up a vault with initVault under tmpdir('nonce-persist-') with remote.enabled true. Enroll a remote-computer with deviceKeygen() through DeviceRegistry.enroll with a permissive policy, then close the Vault. Spawn `node src/server/main.mjs --root <root> --port <free port>` with HOME and MEMEV_CONFIG_DIR set to temp directories, and wait for /healthz. POST /mcp tools/list with signRequest headers and x-forwarded-for, and expect 200. On that 200, send SIGKILL at once (no SIGTERM, no delay) and wait for the exit. Respawn on the same root and replay the identical headers and body. Assert 401, error 'device_key' and error_description matching /already used/, with the message 'replayed after restart'. after() kills every child.

criteria.statement: Test 'rotated token does not reopen' (in process). Enroll a remote-computer; send A with token T1 (200) and keep A's x-memev-ts, x-memev-nonce, x-memev-sig and body. Call v.devices.rotate(v.tokens, deviceId) to get T2. Close the server and Vault, reopen, createServer.
